donor_domain: algebraic topology (sheaf theory); constraint satisfaction; applied probability
donor_source_ids: sheaf theory gluing (Bredon/Godement textbook form); CSP consistency theory (Dechter 2003 survey form); Markov chain lumpability (Kemeny-Snell 1960)
donor_structure: Sheaf gluing: local sections on an open cover that agree on all pairwise overlaps glue to a unique global section (exactness of the section/restriction complex). CSP: k-consistency hierarchy - pairwise (arc) consistency does not imply global satisfiability; higher-order consistency needed. Lumpability: a Markov chain projects to a quotient chain iff transition rates are consistent across each block (block-level congruence).
target_structure: local-to-global consistency of the search state: locally consistent fragments (per-context state updates, per-module views, per-task constraints) vs existence of one globally coherent state; when do local checks certify a global object.
mapping: open cover -> family of contexts/modules/tasks; local section -> per-context state fragment; overlap agreement -> pairwise compatibility of fragments on shared variables; global section -> globally coherent search state; Cech/exactness stage -> k-consistency level; lumping congruence -> quotient-state consistency under state aggregation.
preserved_relations: gluing iff agreement-on-overlaps (sheaf case): exactness gives a clean iff at the sheaf level
hierarchy gap: pairwise compatibility is strictly weaker than global existence in discrete settings (CSP higher-order counterexamples carry over verbatim)
projection consistency: quotient/aggregated state is a valid state process iff the dynamics are block-congruent (lumpability condition transfers)
known_broken_relations: sheaf exactness fails in general for non-sheaf-like (aspherical) constraint systems - the HSG state space has no a priori topology making restriction maps exact
finite consistency checks cannot certify global consistency in general (CSP intractability barrier): no finite k suffices uniformly
dynamic locality (G14 cone) is NOT overlap locality: consistency of fragments is about agreement, the cone is about causal reach - the two can disagree (separate atom)
unknown_correspondences: whether HSG constitutions can be equipped with a topology in which state fragments form an actual sheaf (versus only a pseudo-functor/gluing-on-the-nose) is unexamined
cost of k-th order consistency checks vs burden charge - no donor-owned economics
assumptions_added: fragments are specified on overlapping context families with explicit intersection data
consistency is exact (no approximate gluing / epsilon-consistency considered here)
candidate_theorem: Local fragments glue to a global state iff the consistency complex is exact at the overlap stage; in discrete/algorithmic settings pairwise consistency does not suffice (CSP-type counterexamples), and quotient-state consistency holds iff the transition kernel is block-congruent (lumpability).
strongest_parent: sheaf gluing exactness (textbook standard) + CSP k-consistency hierarchy (standard) + Kemeny-Snell lumpability (standard)
route: L2 structural read; validation by checking all three donor families instantiate the same 'local agreement vs global existence' pattern with matching failure modes
status_rationale: three independent disciplines carry the same iff-condition with standard parent forms; no counterexample to the unified statement found; the 'no uniform finite k' barrier is inherited from CSP and recorded as a broken relation, not a defect of the mapping.
